title: SOURCE_TARGETS validated: chunkWorker Close must close index writer after data writer close error

payload.validation_scope: chunkWorker owns both dataWriter and indexWriter. Current code returned immediately when dataWriter.Close failed, so indexWriter.Close was skipped. The local fix preserves the first/root error and still closes the index writer.
payload.user_symptom: An IMPORT INTO/global-sort external write can return the data-writer close error while skipping terminal Close for the index writer. The user sees the import fail, but index-side buffered KV may not be flushed/closed and writer summaries or cleanup hooks are not reached.
payload.quality_gate: Medium product severity because the root error is visible, but strong methodology evidence because the oracle observes both error identity and terminal action completion. This is a current-source bug, not a replay of the S3 multipart case.

provenance.source: current TiDB source plus RED/GREEN local observer test

name: Multi-writer terminal Close after peer Close error

setup: create or observe two sibling terminal owners under one higher-level operation
append or stage work into both owners
inject a deterministic root error into the first terminal owner
payload.workload: call the higher-level terminal action and observe both the returned root error and every sibling terminal action
controls: the injected root error is returned or preserved
the sibling owner has a direct terminal observer such as onClose, close count, flush log, abort/complete API count, or persisted summary
payload.red: the first root error is returned but a sibling terminal owner is skipped, or the sibling terminal action succeeds/commits when it should abort
payload.green: the root error is preserved and every sibling terminal owner reaches the expected terminal action

rationale: the target was selected by looking for a root error followed by a terminal Close/Flush/Commit action whose state action could be skipped or misclassified
the oracle checks both root error preservation and index writer terminal Close completion
the bug requires two owned terminal writers where one close error must not skip the sibling close
the injected data writer Close error lands exactly before index writer terminal Close
the schedule is fail one terminal writer, then continue the worker Close path
the broad error-identity oracle becomes actionable only after adding terminal action observers for all owned writers

lessons.selector_worked: The terminal-action lane found a current bug by adding an action observer to a broad error-identity obligation.
lessons.oracle_upgrade: Checking final error text alone would miss the bug because the root data writer error is returned; the useful oracle also counts whether the sibling terminal writer was closed.
lessons.quality_note: This is a cleanup/terminal action correctness bug. It is user-visible as an import failure plus skipped index-side terminal close, not a silent successful wrong result.

experimental_patch: chunkWorker.Close records the first dataWriter.Close error instead of returning immediately
if indexWriter.Close also fails, the first/root data error remains the returned error

evidence.green_observation: worker.Close returned the root data writer error and index writer reached flush/close/onClose exactly once

lessons.fix_shape: Accumulate the first Close error while continuing terminal Close on sibling writers; return the first/root error at the end.
lessons.method_note: For multi-owner cleanup, RED requires two observations: root error identity and terminal-action reachability for each owned resource.
lessons.follow_up: Promote a source-target rule for multi-writer Close/Flush/Commit functions where the first terminal error currently causes an early return before sibling owners close.
